subject: plot refreshes a 2nd time on initial page load only

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: plot refreshes a 2nd time on initial page load only
parts:
Toy example is here: 
https://gist.github.com/tcash21/6528653

When I load up my application, I have a progress indicator that spins as I'm querying Amazon Redshift. The data is retrieved, progress indicator disappears, and my ggplot shows up as well as the datatables table below. Then suddenly only the ggplot refreshes, while the datatables data stays in tact. 

I added a Sys.Sleep(1) command so it's easier to see on initial page load. My AWS query is about 20 seconds long so it's much more noticeable on my production app.

Is this because I'm calling getData() in both output$chart and output$table? Is there a best practice way of doing this? I'd assume throwing globally scoped variables around would be frowned upon.

Thank you!

The problem is that the plot refreshes twice on its own on startup.
I've replicated it with just R base plot and tables as well so it's
not specific to the chart or table types. If I remove the table
output, which makes a call to getData(), the problem goes away so I
think it has to do with the multiple getData() calls but do not know
of an elegant way around it.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: plot refreshes a 2nd time on initial page load only
parts:
My guess is that when the page initially loads there is not a vertical scrollbar on the page, and when the data is rendered then a vertical scrollbar appears, changing the size of the container that the plot sits in, which causes it to re-render. Does that sound plausible?

If so, you can use this CSS to make the problem go away:

tags$style(type="text/css", "body { overflow-y: scroll; }")

It will force the scrollbar to appear even when it is not needed.

I have the same problem, but for me it happens to all charts and tables on the page. I believe it has to do with the the chart starting to render before the inputs are rendered. Once the input renders it invalidates the chart and so it re-renders. How do I validate that an input has loaded. 

I have this code:
validate(need(!is.null(input$my_dropdown), "loading data...")

But it does not work because my dropdown does not have a value selected by default. So its always null and stops the chart from rendering. 

I want:
validate(need(is.rendered(input$my_dropdown), "loading data...")
